name: Ann Arbor Public Schools
calendarType: District calendar with level-specific report-writing half days, separate semester and trimester high-school exam tracks, transition days, testing late starts, and distinct first-day and last-day release times
seoTitle: Ann Arbor Public Schools Calendar: AAPS Dates & PDFs
seoDescription: Reviewed AAPS calendar dates, half days, breaks, testing late starts, transition days, separate high-school exam tracks, bell times, translations, and PDFs.
districtFact: The AAPS calendar cannot be reduced to one list of days off. Community, Huron, and Pioneer follow semester-exam windows while Pathways and Skyline use trimester-exam windows; elementary, K-8, middle, and high school students also receive different half-day instructions on report-writing and transition dates.

about.title: Two High-School Exam Rhythms Share One Calendar
about.content: Community, Huron, and Pioneer are grouped under semester exams, while Pathways and Skyline are grouped under trimester exams. Their November, January, March, and June windows do not line up, so a generic 'high-school exams' entry can send a family to the wrong schedule.

about.title: Report-Writing Half Days Stop at Grade-Band Lines
about.content: AAPS repeatedly gives elementary, K-8, and middle-school students a half day for report writing while high-school students attend a full day. The May report-writing date narrows again to elementary and K-8, leaving both middle and high school on a full day.

about.title: Transition Days and Half Days Are Paired but Not Identical
about.content: The spring calendar pairs an eighth-grade transition day with a high-school half day, then a fifth-grade transition day with a middle-school half day. The visiting grade and the shortened school level are both important; neither label should be dropped.

about.title: The First and Last Half Days Use Different Clocks
about.content: The official bell table separates first-day and report-writing half-day release times from last-day release times. In 2026-27, high schools release at 11:00 a.m. on the first-day schedule but at 9:40 a.m. on the last day; K-5 shifts from 11:50 a.m. to 11:35 a.m.

about.title: The Calendar Is Also a Transportation Document
about.content: AAPS returned to a three-tier bus schedule for 2025-26, moving elementary start and release times five minutes while leaving Westerman Preschool, K-8, middle, and high-school times unchanged. That change explains why archived bell times should not be carried into a later year without checking.

about.title: Preschool and A2Virtual Sit Outside the Main Track
about.content: Both reviewed PDFs warn that preschools and A2Virtual follow slightly different calendars. The districtwide K-12 overview is the baseline for neighborhood schools, not a substitute for preschool session calendars, virtual-course terms, or required A2Virtual proctoring dates.

calendarNotes: AAPS combines districtwide attendance dates with several grade-band and program-specific schedules. The first and last days are half days for all students, but their release times differ by level and by whether the date is the first/report-writing schedule or the final-day schedule. Elementary, K-8, and middle-school report-writing dates often leave high schools on a full day, while the May report-writing half day applies only to elementary and K-8 students. Community, Huron, and Pioneer use semester exam windows; Pathways and Skyline use trimester exam windows. Spring transition days pair eighth graders with a high-school half day and fifth graders with a middle-school half day. Testing dates can create late starts only for named grades rather than the whole district. Preschool and A2Virtual calendars remain separate, and the current 2026-27 calendar hub also provides Arabic, Chinese, Dari, Japanese, Korean, and Spanish editions. Families should use the live AAPS calendar, bell-schedule page, and school site for changes, transportation, commencement, athletics, and program-specific dates.

planningTips.title: Planning with the AAPS Calendar
content: Match every half day to the listed school levels; high school may remain full day when elementary, K-8, and middle school dismiss early.
Use the correct half-day column: first-day and report-writing releases are later than last-day releases for most grade bands.
Check whether the student attends Community, Huron, or Pioneer on a semester track, or Pathways or Skyline on a trimester track.
Read testing entries by grade because PSAT, SAT, Work Readiness, and late-start instructions apply to different student groups.
Keep both parts of each transition-day entry: the transitioning grade and the school level receiving the half day.
Use the translated 2026-27 PDF that is most accessible to the household; all six translated editions are linked from the official calendar hub.
Check preschool and A2Virtual pages separately, and confirm school-level events, transportation, weather closures, and commencement dates in the live calendar.

livingHere.intro: AAPS serves Ann Arbor and surrounding Washtenaw County communities through neighborhood schools, K-8 options, comprehensive and alternative high schools, virtual learning, preschool, and specialty pathways. Those choices create real calendar differences inside the district.

highlights.label: Two academic cycles
highlights.detail: Community, Huron, and Pioneer use semester exams; Pathways and Skyline use trimester exams.

highlights.label: Two K-8 options
highlights.detail: Ann Arbor Open and A2 STEAM follow the K-8 bell and half-day categories rather than the K-5 or middle-school row.

highlights.label: K-12 IB pathway
highlights.detail: AAPS identifies International Baccalaureate programming at Mitchell, Scarlett, and Huron across primary, middle, diploma, and career-related years.

highlights.label: A2Virtual grades 6-12
highlights.detail: The district's online option has course terms and proctoring events that can differ from the printed K-12 overview.

highlights.label: Separate preschool calendar
highlights.detail: AAPS directs preschool families to their program or school website instead of treating the main PDF as complete.

highlights.label: Six translated editions
highlights.detail: The 2026-27 calendar hub publishes Arabic, Chinese, Dari, Japanese, Korean, and Spanish PDFs.

districtFaqs.q: When does Ann Arbor Public Schools start in 2026-27?
districtFaqs.a: Students start Monday, August 31, 2026, on a half-day schedule. Release time depends on school level: 11:00 a.m. for high school, 11:15 a.m. for middle and K-8, 11:50 a.m. for K-5, and 11:25 a.m. for the listed PK programs.

districtFaqs.q: Do all AAPS schools have the same report-writing half days?
districtFaqs.a: No. October and March half days apply to elementary, K-8, and middle schools while high schools remain full day. The May report-writing half day applies only to elementary and K-8; middle and high schools remain full day.

districtFaqs.q: Why are there two AAPS high-school exam schedules?
districtFaqs.a: Community, Huron, and Pioneer use semester exam windows. Pathways and Skyline use trimester exam windows, so their November and March dates differ even though all five schools can share June exam dates.

districtFaqs.q: What time does AAPS dismiss on the last day?
districtFaqs.a: The 2026-27 PDF lists 9:40 a.m. for high school, 10:45 a.m. for middle school, 10:50 a.m. for K-8, and 11:35 a.m. for K-5. These are earlier than the first-day and report-writing half-day releases.

districtFaqs.q: Does A2Virtual follow the AAPS district calendar?
districtFaqs.a: Not exactly. The official overview says A2Virtual follows a slightly different calendar. Virtual students should check the A2Virtual calendar for course start and end dates, required proctoring, summer terms, and program notices.

districtFaqs.q: Does AAPS publish translated school calendars?
districtFaqs.a: Yes. For 2026-27, the official calendar page links Arabic, Chinese, Dari, Japanese, Korean, and Spanish PDF editions in addition to the English printable and text versions.

districtFaqs.q: Are AAPS preschool dates included in the main PDF?
districtFaqs.a: No. Both reviewed district PDFs say preschools follow a slightly different calendar. Families should use the preschool program or school site for session dates, attendance days, and bell schedules.

customSections.label: One Half Day, Two Release-Time Columns
customSections.content: The 2026-27 PDF publishes different release times for the first day/report-writing half days and the last day. These are planning times, not a promise that every program follows the district row.

table.footnote: Community afternoon end times vary by student schedule; other preschool programs use their school-specific bell schedules.

customSections.label: AAPS High-School Exam Tracks
customSections.content: The named schools share district breaks but do not share one grading rhythm. The calendar's exact school grouping matters whenever exams are listed.

customSections.label: Where the District Overview Stops
customSections.content: The one-page PDF covers districtwide school-year dates, named testing and exam windows, and standard bell times. It does not replace the separate preschool or A2Virtual calendar, a school's event calendar, commencement updates, transportation notices, or weather-closure messages.
